brief: Nomura's McElligott flags aggregate SPX dealer gamma at negative $7.3bn, the deepest since January 2019, producing a two-way market that rallies sharply then gives it back. This lands before a 'Risk Quad-fecta': NVDA earnings, VIX expiration, the Anthropic IPO and monthly OpEx. He argues there is no fuel for a VIX blowout (leveraged VIX ETN assets and vega-to-buy both near multi-year lows), but a fat-tails list (Fed hawkish repricing via a Warsh-era turf war, an Iran supply shock, AI capex debt supply, the wealth effect) keeps downside risk 'amorphous.' A second thread: Nvidia's 'Central Bank of AI' put is impaired after Jensen Huang's resignation, CFO Kress as interim CEO, and China revenue reset to zero, explaining a -35% stock move. Professional positioning is washed out (low leverage, heavy selling) while 401(k)/retail flows hit record highs, sustaining 'buy-the-dip' — a dynamic McElligott warns flips to 'Sellers are Lower' if NVDA or the Anthropic IPO stumble into $82bn of mechanical selling.
